findings.description: Static AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded as plaintext Lambda environment variables in the Terraform code. These credentials are stored in version control and in the Terraform state, and are visible to anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, allowing credential theft and account compromise.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so Lambda environment variables (which here contain secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are shown in plaintext in the console/API rather than being protected by a customer-managed CMK with restricted key policy.
The function does not set code_signing_config_arn, so no signature verification is performed on the deployment package, allowing tampered or untrusted code to be deployed.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is deprecated and no longer receives security patches, leaving the execution environment exposed to known unpatched vulnerabilities.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security-group or NACL controls, which eases data exfiltration if the function is compromised.
